title: Investigation Murray: An investigation into allegations of corrupt conduct by the Mayor of Townsville

summary.label: Generated summary: written by an AI model from the report text and checked against the cited pages.

sentences.text: Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission investigated complaints about the then Mayor of Townsville.
The investigation covered a chief executive’s severance payment, allegedly misleading election claims, alleged conduct towards councillors and alleged disclosure of confidential council information.
The CCC concluded that the mayor acted within his lawful authority over the chief executive’s departure and severance payment, requiring no further action on that complaint.
The CCC reported referring evidence from the election-claims and confidential-information investigations to the Director of Public Prosecutions for advice.
The CCC recommended a legislative review covering candidate disclosures, false election claims, private advisers, council information and disciplinary processes after councillors leave office.

items.quote: Mr Thompson’s actions in terminating the employment of the former CEO, including the payment of any relevant severance payments, were found to be within the scope of his lawful authority.

While the current system regulates the appointment and provision of advisors to councillors, the current regulatory framework fails to adequately address the significant corruption risks associated with the engagement of advisors by councillors who are independent of and unknown to Council.
